name: shopify-store-sync-mcp

tools.name: list_stores
tools.description: List the Shopify stores this server can reach, with their write permissions. Also gives this server's version. Secrets are never returned.

tools.name: list_resource_types
tools.description: Describe each resource type that can be snapshotted, diffed and synced, how items are keyed, and which are read by default.

tools.name: snapshot_store
tools.description: Read configuration from one store (or a snapshot folder) and return it in the response, in portable form (IDs replaced by handles). Returns counts and keys; set full=true to include the data. Writes nothing; to save the configuration to files, use export_snapshot.

store.description: Store alias, or "dir:<path>" for a snapshot folder made with export_snapshot.

resources.description: Resource types to include. Default: metafield_definitions, metaobject_definitions, collections, pages, shop_policies, metaobjects, menus, redirects. products, metafields and translations are opt-in.

owner_types.description: Metafield owner types. For metafield_definitions, default: PRODUCT, PRODUCTVARIANT, COLLECTION, CUSTOMER, ORDER, DRAFTORDER, COMPANY, COMPANY_LOCATION, LOCATION, MARKET, PAGE, BLOG, ARTICLE, SHOP. For metafield values (metafields): PRODUCT, COLLECTION, PRODUCTVARIANT, SHOP (all by default).

metaobject_types.description: Limit metaobjects to these types. Default: all non-reserved types.

namespaces.description: Limit metafield values (metafields) to these namespaces.

locales.description: Limit translations to these locales, e.g. ["fr", "de"]. Default: every non-primary locale.

prices.description: products: also copy variant prices and compare-at prices. Off by default, since prices usually differ per store.

inventory.description: products: also copy stock, the available quantity per location, into the target's location with the same name. Off by default. Needs read_inventory and read_locations (and write_inventory to write): run connect again if the sign-in is older.

as_drafts.description: Leave the published state alone: new pages are created hidden and new metaobject entries as drafts, existing ones keep their state. Products are always created as drafts.

include.description: Only keys matching one of these globs, e.g. ["PRODUCT.custom.*", "faq/*", "fr:*"].

exclude.description: Drop keys matching any of these globs.

include_reserved.description: metafield_definitions: also compare Shopify-reserved ones (namespace "shopify", the category metafields that drive storefront filters). Compared only: a plan reports them as conflicts and never writes them.

full.description: Include each item's data (can be large).

tools.name: export_snapshot
tools.description: Save a store's configuration to a folder on disk as one JSON file per item (sorted keys, no store IDs), ready to commit to git. Returns only a summary; to look at the configuration in the response, use snapshot_store. Use "dir:<path>" as the source of diff_stores or plan_sync to compare or restore from it. Only writes local files, never to Shopify.

dir.description: Folder to write, inside the snapshot base folder (SYNC_SNAPSHOT_DIR, or the folder the server runs in). Must be empty, new, or an earlier snapshot folder (its item files are replaced).

tools.name: diff_stores
tools.description: Compare configuration between a source and a target: what exists only in the source, what differs (field by field), and what exists only in the target. Either side can be a snapshot folder ("dir:<path>"), e.g. to check whether production drifted from the committed config. Read-only.

source.description: Store alias, or "dir:<path>" for a snapshot folder made with export_snapshot.

target.description: Store alias, or "dir:<path>" for a snapshot folder made with export_snapshot.

limit.description: Max items listed per section (default 100, markdown 50). The counts always cover everything.

format.description: "markdown" returns a report to paste into a ticket or an email.

tools.name: compare_item
tools.description: Compare a single item between two stores, side by side: whether each has it, every field that differs (entry by entry inside JSON values), and whether the items it points at (products, pages, metaobjects...) exist in the target. Reads only that item where possible, so it is quick. Use it for a targeted check instead of a full diff. Read-only.

source.description: Store alias, or "dir:<path>" for a snapshot folder made with export_snapshot.

target.description: Store alias, or "dir:<path>" for a snapshot folder made with export_snapshot.

key.description: The item's key, as diff_stores lists it: "size_guide/shirts" (metaobjects), "faq" (pages), "PRODUCT.custom.fabric" (metafield_definitions)...

tools.name: plan_sync
tools.description: Build a dry-run plan that would make the target store match the source (a store or a snapshot folder) for the selected resources: creates, updates, conflicts, files to upload and references missing in the target. Nothing is written. Returns a plan_id for apply_plan.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Show a previously created sync plan. With no plan_id, list recent plans.

format.description: "markdown" returns the plan as a report, to share before applying it.

tools.name: apply_plan
tools.description: Write a reviewed plan to the target store. Refused unless the target has allowWrites=true. For a protected store the person is asked to confirm in the client (or applies from the command line); the assistant can't confirm on their behalf. Re-reads the target first and skips anything that changed since planning. Uploads missing files. Creates and updates only, never deletes. Every op is written to an audit log.

confirm.description: Leave empty. Only read when the server runs with SYNC_ALLOW_AGENT_CONFIRM=true (unattended automation); otherwise a protected store is confirmed by the person, not by this argument.

only.description: Apply only these op seq numbers.

wait.description: Wait for the whole apply before returning. By default a plan of more than 50 steps (SYNC_BACKGROUND_STEPS) runs in the background and this returns at once; follow it with apply_status.

tools.name: apply_status
tools.description: How far an apply has got: steps created, updated, skipped, failed and left per resource type, the current phase, progress inside a Shopify bulk operation, time so far and an estimate of the time left, failures counted per resource type and reason, and the latest failures. Also answers for an apply that ended or was interrupted by a server restart. With no plan_id, the most recent apply.

failures.description: How many of the latest failures to list (default 20).

resource.description: List only the failures of this resource type, e.g. products.

tools.name: cancel_apply
tools.description: Stop an apply that is running in the background: no further step is started and the Shopify bulk operations it started are cancelled. What was already written stays written (nothing is rolled back or deleted). Also stops bulk operations left running by an apply whose server was restarted. Follow with apply_status, then plan_sync to see what is left.

plan_id.description: The plan being applied. Default: the most recent apply.

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: Read what apply_plan wrote: the most recent audit log entries, newest first, one per step (plan, target store, resource type, key, outcome and message). Filter by plan, outcome (created, updated, skipped, failed) or resource type. Read-only; the log is a local file and nothing is read from Shopify.

resource.description: Only entries of this resource type.

limit.description: Max entries returned (default 50). matched counts them all.

tools.name: diff_themes
tools.description: Read-only comparison of theme configuration between two stores: JSON templates, section groups and settings_data.json (default files: templates/*.json, sections/*.json, config/settings_data.json). Compares the published themes unless theme ids are given. Never writes to a theme. Needs read_themes.

ignore_settings.description: Settings to leave out, as globs on their path, optionally limited to files: ["current.sections.header.*", "config/settings_data.json:current.color_*"]. Use it to quiet settings that differ on purpose between stores.

format.description: "markdown" returns a report to paste into a ticket or an email.

instructions: Syncs configuration between Shopify stores. Use this order: list_stores to see the stores and which accept writes, diff_stores (or compare_item for one item) to see what differs, plan_sync to build a dry-run plan, show the plan to the person, then apply_plan only after they approve it. Nothing is written to Shopify except by apply_plan, and it never deletes. A protected store asks the person to confirm; never try to confirm for them. Large applies run in the background: follow them with apply_status, stop them with cancel_apply, and read what was written with get_audit_log. snapshot_store returns a store's configuration in the response; export_snapshot saves it to files for git instead.
